sections.h2: Which Flint offices deal with a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Flint splits the job three ways: the city's Assessments Division picks the value, the city treasury sends and collects the bill, and the Genesee County Treasurer inherits anything still unpaid after the March 1 handoff.

The Assessments Division also handles property transfer affidavits, principal residence exemptions, land splits and combinations. Genesee County's equalization office maintains parcel descriptions everywhere in the county except Flint, so a Flint lot-line or split question goes to city hall at 810-766-7255, the number printed on the assessments page.

  • Value and exemptions: City of Flint Assessments Division.
  • Current bill: City of Flint, payable through InvoiceCloud from the city's online services page, where a BS&A portal also looks up parcels.
  • Delinquent bill: Genesee County Treasurer, 324 S Saginaw St Ste 2A, weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00.

Flint is a compact city with low home values, and both facts shape what a tax bill means to an owner there. About 79,306 people lived in Flint as of July 2025, down from 81,252 in 2020. The city sits on 33.44 square miles of land along the Flint River, 66 miles from Detroit.

With a midpoint value of $53,500, an overdue balance of even a few thousand dollars can take a large share of a sale price. Ask for an exact payoff early.

sections.h2: What value Flint taxes your house on
sections.html:
Flint taxes a figure called taxable value, which starts from an assessed value set at half of the city's estimate of true cash value. The estimate draws on two years of local sales and property data.

A sale changes the arithmetic. The year after a transfer, taxable value is reset up to the assessed value, a step the Flint assessor calls uncapping. Starting with the second year after the sale, increases are held to the lesser of 5% or the inflation multiplier, apart from new construction.

Two things follow for a seller. The bill you have carried may run well below the one your buyer gets, and a buyer whose lender escrows taxes should expect a higher monthly payment. Mentioning that early prevents a sour surprise after closing.

sections.h2: How to challenge a Flint assessment
sections.html:
Only in March. The Notice of Assessment arrives at the end of February, headed with a line saying it is no tax bill, and it lists the board's meeting dates.

Once the March Board of Review adjourns, the city's assessors have no legal power to alter the number. Commercial and industrial owners may skip the board and petition the Michigan Tax Tribunal by May 31. For homes, state law sets July 31 of the tax year as the tribunal deadline, after a protest at the board. The city has at times accepted notarized letters, with original signatures and supporting papers, in place of a visit, so ask the assessor what the coming year allows.

  • Hardship relief: the online services page lists a low-income hardship application called HOPE.
  • Disabled veteran owners: file an affidavit with the assessor along with the explanation of benefits.
  • Principal residence exemption: the owner must live in the home by June 1. It lifts 18 mills of school operating tax. Tell the city when you move out, because skipping that step can bring a denial with penalties.

The dates printed on your Flint bill rule, since the city bills on its own calendar. If no bill reached you, contact the city.

Behind the city's calendar sit two state rules. The summer levy attaches to the property on July 1, and summer tax collected with city taxes takes the same penalties as the city's other charges. Any balance left on March 1 is handed to the county treasurer as delinquent, at which point a 4% county fee and interest of 1% a month begin.

sections.h2: Where an unpaid Flint bill ends up
sections.html:
At the county, and after about three years the parcel can be foreclosed and auctioned. Here is Michigan's schedule for county foreclosing units.

  • Year one, March 1: the unpaid bill is returned to the county and the 4% fee and monthly interest start to build.
  • Year two, March 1: the parcel forfeits, a $175 title fee goes on, and redemption carries half a percent a month counted from the prior March 1.
  • Year three, March 30 and 31: the circuit court must enter its judgment by the 30th, and the 31st is the final day to redeem before title moves to the county.
  • After that: public agencies get a first chance to buy, then online auctions run. Genesee County holds several rounds each fall.

A former owner whose house sold at auction for more than the taxes and costs may be able to claim the surplus. Ask the Genesee County Treasurer what the claim process requires.

sections.h2: Selling a Flint house that owes tax
sections.html:
You can. The title company requests a payoff from the city or county, adds interest and fees through the closing date, and subtracts the total from your proceeds.

The seller also owes transfer tax: $3.75 per $500 of price to the state, plus 55 cents per $500 to the county, which applies to any Michigan county under two million residents, Genesee included. Both go to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed. Foreclosure transfers, deeds to a child or grandchild and land contracts that keep title with the seller are among the listed exemptions.

Two city filings follow a sale. File a property transfer affidavit with the assessor, and if you took the principal residence exemption, file a rescission. When back taxes, repairs or a tenant make a listing slow, a cash purchase as-is lets the payoff come out in one step at the table.

A simple order of work for an owner with a balance:

  1. Find out whether the bill is with the city or has moved to Genesee County.
  2. Request a payoff that runs to your expected closing date.
  3. Give it to the title company so it can deduct the amount from your proceeds.
  4. After closing, file the transfer affidavit and the exemption rescission with the assessor.

faqs.q: Who gets my payment on a current Flint tax bill?
faqs.a: The City of Flint takes it, online through InvoiceCloud or by the methods on the bill. After a balance moves to the county on March 1, you pay the Genesee County Treasurer at 324 S Saginaw St Ste 2A instead.

faqs.q: Is a residential assessment open to challenge after March?
faqs.a: No. Flint's value becomes final when the March Board of Review closes. Commercial and industrial owners are the exception and can petition the Michigan Tax Tribunal directly by May 31.

faqs.q: Why did my Flint taxes jump after a purchase?
faqs.a: Taxable value resets to assessed value in the year after a sale, which can raise the bill sharply. The assessor suggests calling your lender if the tax is escrowed, since the payment may need to change.

faqs.q: Does a Flint buyer take on my unpaid tax?
faqs.a: The tax is a lien on the parcel under state law, so it must be cleared for the buyer to get clean title. A title company usually pays it out of the seller's proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Who writes the transfer tax check on a Flint sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. Michigan sets $3.75 per $500 for the state and 55 cents per $500 for the county, and the money goes to the county treasurer within 15 days of the deed's delivery.
